trace.notes: Mapped the paper from the table of contents on page 2. Major sections are: introduction; basics of public key cryptography; free group cryptography; public key exchange using nonabelian groups; Shamir three-pass and key transport; digital signatures, authentication and password security; braid group cryptography and platform groups; cryptography with polycyclic groups; generic complexity and asymptotic density; the generic free group property; and open problems.

Definitions and theorem-like material occur mainly in Sections 4, 8, 9, and 10, including Definitions 4.1-4.4 on page 13 and Theorems 10.1-10.7 on pages 25-27. The likely open-problem region is Section 11, pages 27-28.
Section 1 provides survey motivation and announces that a list of open problems will appear later; no standalone research question was accepted from this section.
Section 2 is background on classical public-key cryptography and introduces no standalone open problem.
Section 3 surveys free-group cryptography and mentions ongoing complexity study of Reidemeister-Schreier rewriting, but the explicit open formulation is deferred to Section 11 and captured there.
Section 4 defines several group-theoretic problems used in cryptography but does not state standalone open questions outside the later open-problems list.
Section 5 describes key transport protocols and candidate platform groups; no standalone open problem was accepted from this section.
Section 6 surveys digital signatures, authentication, and password verification. Its unresolved directions are captured explicitly in Section 11 rather than as standalone questions here.
Section 7 surveys braid-group cryptography and desired platform properties, but the explicit platform-selection questions are listed in Section 11.

Section 8 states that the complexity of the search conjugacy problem in polycyclic groups is unknown and conjectured to be exponential; Section 11 provides the explicit complexity questions accepted in this run.
Section 9 is conceptual background on generic complexity and asymptotic density; no standalone open question was extracted from it.
Section 10 presents results on the generic free group property and no standalone open question beyond the later Section 11 list.

Section 11 contains the paper's explicit open-problems list. Nineteen candidate questions were extracted from the General, Complexity Analysis and Security, Quantum Algorithms and Quantum Complexity, and Implementation subsections.
